criteria.criterion: The CHANGELOG entry (CHANGELOG.md, under Fixed) and code comment name the root cause: the stored tail was taken of the whole CI log, which ends with post-job cleanup, and failure lines were not selected.
criteria.evidence: I read the diff. A new bullet under `## [Unreleased]` / `### Fixed` (the Unreleased heading is at CHANGELOG.md:8, the 0.1.0 heading at :3532) says `detail_from_job_logs` "took the tail of the whole CI job log, which ends with the runner's post-job cleanup ... and never selected the failure lines". Doc comments on detail_from_job_logs (client.rs:249-251), without_post_job_cleanup and failure_tail (checks.rs) state the same cause.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core detail_from_job_logs`: a new test feeds a job log with a failing test and a trailing post-job cleanup block (Post job cleanup, git config --unset-all, Cleaning up orphan processes, a Node.js deprecation warning) and asserts output_tail contains the `FAILED`/`panicked at` lines and no cleanup text. It fails on the base commit and passes with the change.
criteria.evidence: detail_from_job_logs_drops_the_post_job_cleanup_tail passes. Its log ends with the four planned cleanup lines (CLEANUP in gh/tests.rs). It asserts that output_tail contains `panicked at`, `test tests::a ... FAILED`, ` right: 2` and `test result: FAILED`, contains no cleanup text, and holds the panic within its last 600 chars and last 60 lines. Fails on base: I did not run this; it is inferred from the base code. Base used `tail_lines(&text, 200)` on the whole log. This log is about 21 lines, so the cleanup lines would stay in the tail and `assert_no_cleanup` would fail. Athena's own revert demonstration exited 101, but because the new checks.rs unit tests did not compile against base, not because an assertion failed.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core detail_from_job_logs`: a new test with a log that yields no parsed test names (a shard that did not finish, or non-cargo test output) followed by cleanup asserts output_tail keeps the lines containing `test result`, `FAILED`, `failures:` or `panicked at` rather than only cleanup text. It fails before the change and passes after, so it covers the class and not one job.
criteria.evidence: Two tests pass. detail_from_job_logs_keeps_failure_lines_when_no_test_is_named has no `Running` line and the conclusion `cancelled`. Its failure lines are followed by 250 progress lines and the cleanup block. It asserts that `panicked at`, `assertion failed: ok`, `test result: FAILED` and `failures:` are kept, with no cleanup text and the panic near the end. detail_from_job_logs_keeps_a_failing_unit_behind_passing_units covers a failing unit followed by 250 passing tests. On base the last 200 lines would be progress or passing lines plus cleanup, so the `panicked at` assertions would fail (inferred from the base code, not run). This matches the real f6x6 log in the evidence snapshot (brief-verifier.md:190-216): a passing xtask unit, then `Post job cleanup.` and git config lines.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core checks`: existing tests for tail_lines, 200-line and byte caps, FAILING_UNITS_PREFIX and redaction still pass, and a log with no failure lines and no cleanup keeps its plain tail as before.
criteria.evidence: `checks`: 71 passed, 0 failed. This includes tail_lines_keeps_the_last_n_lines_and_the_final_newline, a_failed_run_keeps_its_last_200_lines..., a_failed_runs_kept_lines_stop_at_the_byte_ceiling, and the new failure_tail_is_the_plain_tail_without_failure_outside_the_end, which checks that output equals tail_lines for a plain log, a passing-only log and a log whose panic is at the end. `gh::`: 126 passed, including red_reused_run_records_failing_tests_and_log_tail (the units header), red_reused_run_redacts_the_log_before_recording and reused_red_degrades_when_the_log_lists_no_failures.

findings.summary: No run showed the new gh tests failing on base; Athena's revert demonstration failed only because the code did not compile.
findings.evidence: The fails-without-2/3 record exited 101 with E0425 errors: the new checks.rs unit tests reference without_post_job_cleanup and failure_tail, which do not exist on base. So no run showed the gh tests failing their assertions. Reading the base code (tail_lines on the whole log) shows they would fail, but this was not demonstrated.

findings.summary: A failure block keeps only the marker line plus at most 4 following lines.
findings.evidence: A panic with a long custom message, or a backtrace, is cut after 4 lines when the block is moved to the end. Default assert_eq output (message, left, right) fits. Stopping at a blank line or the next `----` header, within the n/2 cap, would keep the whole message.

findings.summary: The failure section changes the order of lines in the stored tail.
findings.evidence: The earlier failure lines are placed after the log's end, behind a separator line. This is documented in the code and is a deliberate trade-off so that end-keeping readers see the failure, but a reader may at first take the moved lines as the last output.

summary: The change passes. It fixes the cause where the bad record was built: `detail_from_job_logs` used to take the last 200 lines of the whole CI log, and that log ends with the runner's cleanup steps. Now each job log is cut before its cleanup block (`Post job cleanup.`, `Cleaning up orphan processes`, `##[group]Post `). When failure lines (`panicked at`, `... FAILED`, `test result: FAILED`, `failures:`, the `---- name stdout ----` header) sit outside the log's last few hundred bytes, they are added after a separator as the last lines of the stored tail, still within the 200-line and byte limits. I checked the cleanup markers against a real stored CI log from job f6x6 in the evidence snapshot, and they match. The three new detail_from_job_logs tests pass. They cover a failing test followed by cleanup, a log where no test name can be read (the shard did not finish), and a failing unit followed by passing units, so the fix covers the class of failure, not one job. All 71 `checks` tests and 126 `gh::` tests pass, including the existing tail-length, byte-limit, unit-header and redaction tests. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and full test checks passed. The scope matches the deliverables list exactly. One gap: no run showed the new tests failing on the base commit. Athena's revert demonstration only failed to compile. Reading the base code shows the tests would fail there, but this was not run. A minor limit: a moved failure block keeps at most 4 lines after its first line, so a long panic message or backtrace is cut.
